Filing is by a licensed company secretary, so the buyer is the CoSec firm. Named incumbents (Sleek, Kaizen, Seed) were not confirmed in Malaysia; 3E CPA style secretarial firms dominate results.

result.competitor: I found no Malaysia-specific ROS/eROSES compliance software in searches in Malay, English and Chinese. eROSES is the free state filing portal. Done-for-you firms such as Bestar Asia offer "Annual Compliance" support for annual returns and audited accounts (fees not shown). Generic membership CRMs exist. Not checked: local accounting firms or company secretaries offering the same service, and whether eROSES auto-fills data from earlier years.
result.duty: Societies Act 1966 s.14(1) (Malaysia, in force): annual statement (penyata tahunan / Borang 9) to the Registrar of Societies through eROSES within 60 days after the AGM. The 60-day rule comes from a 2013 report of the 2012 National Audit and a 2021 RoS statement via secondary sources. I did not open the Act's text. Sanction: an order to provide the information, then deregistration. s.53 sets general fines up to RM5,000 (NST Jul 2026). ROS proposed amendments in Jul 2026 (tougher penalties, possible mandatory audits for NGOs taking public donations); they are not yet tabled. Not reached: whether eROSES pre-fills Borang 9, and any Sabah/Sarawak differences. The Rajah & Tann amendment article is about Singapore, so I excluded it. The 2023 thesun article (the minister telling ROS to act on NGOs not filing financial reports) is dated Dec 2023, not Jul 2026 as the claim says.
result.market: NST May 2024 (ROS): 95,694 registered NGOs, excluding political parties: 85,023 parent societies and 10,671 branches. 14,307 were cancelled in 2021-2023, mainly for not submitting annual reports. Selangor alone has about 2,700 active residents' associations (2023).
result.reason: The duty is real and current. Under Societies Act 1966 s.14(1), societies must file an annual statement with ROS through eROSES within 60 days after the AGM, or 60 days after year-end if no AGM is held. Failing to file can lead to deregistration. ROS cancelled 14,307 societies in 2021-23, mostly for this reason. In 2026 ROS put MTUC under a provisional dissolution order and is weighing mandatory audits. The market is about 85,000 parent societies plus 10,700 branches (2024). I found no Malaysia-specific software for the Borang 9/AGM pack. But it is filed once a year by unpaid treasurers, eROSES is free, and willingness to pay is low. Exposure is clearest for societies handling donations.

result.competitor: No Malaysian vendor found that produces BNM MSB statistical returns or tracks minimum capital funds. Searches were in English and Malay ("perisian/sistem pengurup wang", "money changer POS Malaysia BNM report"). The only product that surfaced was CurrencyXchanger (Clearview Systems, overseas): a POS with AML record-keeping, with no sign it handles BNM returns. BNM's MSSB is an online application and tracking system, not a returns generator; ROMS serves Authorised Dealers only. Principal licensees supply the MSB system to their agents. Local POS vendors may exist without much web presence (not_reached).
result.duty: MSBA 2011 (Act 731), in force. Three duties: s.34(1) statistical reporting under the Guidelines on Statistical Reporting for MSB (5 Feb 2018), with forms attached; s.22(1) minimum capital funds; s.27(1) receipts. Penalties are administrative monetary penalties under s.75(2)(b). Recent cases: RM16,000 on Wang S. Enterprise for late statistical returns (29 Jul 2026); RM1,500-2,000 on each of 13 licensees for capital shortfall Jul-Dec 2025 (25 Feb 2026); RM1,500-3,000 on 10 licensees (Dec 2025); RM17,400 for not issuing receipts (claim, eapn102026, not re-fetched). AML/CFT/TFS customer ID capture also applies to money changers, including transactions under RM3,000. Return frequency is per the guidelines, which I did not open (claimed monthly/yearly).
result.market: BNM's licensed MSB operators page lists licensees and agents but publishes no counts. The claim's 801 licensed money changers was not independently verified. On that basis the market is in the hundreds of mostly small Sdn Bhd money changers (Class A/B), plus approved agents who usually rely on their principal's system.
result.reason: The duty is real and BNM enforces it repeatedly. Under MSBA s.34(1) and the 2018 Statistical Reporting Guidelines, licensees must file statistical returns on time; Wang S. Enterprise paid an RM16,000 penalty on 29 Jul 2026. Under s.22(1) they must hold minimum capital funds; 13 licensees paid RM1,500-2,000 penalties on 25 Feb 2026. Receipts are required under s.27(1). English and Malay searches found no Malaysian vendor that generates BNM returns, only CurrencyXchanger, an overseas product with no sign it handles BNM returns. BNM's MSSB system handles applications and tracking only. The weaknesses: under about 1,000 licensees (801 not verified), some agents get their systems from principal licensees, penalties are small, and local POS vendors may exist that my searches missed.

result.competitor: I found no compliance software for STRA licensing. What exists: Mishu (mishu.my), a licence-agent and guide service for general MBPP and MBSP business licences; the council portals MBPP uLesen and MBSP SPEEDBiz (per third-party guides; I couldn't confirm they handle the TIP licence); and MOTAC TOURLIST for tourist-premise registration. MySTRA and the Penang Homestay Association are lobby groups that are asking for an extension and tiered fees.
result.duty: Private Homestay (Penang Local Authorities) By-Law 2026 (also reported as the Private Short-term Accommodation By-laws 2026). In force since 1 Aug 2026, with a 2-month grace period and enforcement from 1 Nov 2026. It applies to any stay of no more than 6 consecutive months with no tenancy. Licences are annual, from MBPP (island) or MBSP (mainland). Fees: RM50 application, RM1,000 per year for up to 3 rooms plus RM200 per extra room, and an RM1,800 per year TIP fee per unit. Penalty: a fine up to RM2,000 and/or up to 1 year in jail, and councils can shut premises. Licence conditions cover operations, cleanliness, safety and nuisance. Coverage does not mention recurring guest-register or reporting duties (not verified). MBPP bars TIP in all stratified residential property, in named neighbourhoods, and in low-cost housing; George Town heritage rules also apply. MOTAC registration (TOURLIST) is separate and requires the council licence first.
result.market: The Penang Homestay Association estimates 8,000-10,000 operators, not all active (The Star, 7 Sep 2026). The state says it lacks accurate unit data (NST). MBPP's ban on strata residential property removes most island condo units, so the number that can be licensed is much smaller (not quantified). Complaints: 364 to MBPP and 24 to MBSP between 2020 and March 2026.
result.reason: The duty is real. Penang's Private Homestay/Short-term Accommodation By-Law 2026 took effect on 1 Aug 2026 and enforcement starts on 1 Nov. Operators need an annual MBPP or MBSP licence (RM50 application, RM1,000+ licence, RM1,800 TIP fee). Penalties go up to RM2,000 and/or one year in jail. I found no dedicated software, only general licence agents (Mishu) and council portals (MBPP uLesen, MBSP SPEEDBiz). But the job is a once-a-year licence application, and the rush window closes in about three weeks. MBPP bars all strata residential property, which covers most Airbnb condos on the island, so far fewer than the 6,000-10,000 units can be licensed at all. Hosts are already angry about the RM2,850 cost, so they will resist paying more. A done-for-you agent service fits better than software.

result.competitor: MOCCIS SPBK: web-based, bilingual, koperasi-specific accounting and member-loan system that says it complies with SKM financial-statement reporting guidelines and was evaluated by SKM. Its flyer is old and I found no price. p-SKM: free SKM Excel accounting tool from 2014-15; I don't know if it is still maintained. ANGKASA: its recovery division helps dormant koperasi prepare account statements, and with SKM and IKMa it gives free POS and website help. SKM: grant of RM3,000 (Peninsular) or RM3,500 (Sabah/Sarawak) for audit and accounting, plus guidance and training. I found no koperasi compliance or AGM-pack cloud SaaS in Malaysia. memberAMS is generic membership software.
result.duty: Section 61 of the Co-operative Societies Act 1993 (Act 502), restated in SKM guideline GP26 of 1 Sep 2024: accounts must be audited at least once each financial year by an SKM-approved auditor. Koperasi that run no business, hold no AGM and have no audit for more than 3 years face cancellation (SKM Negeri Sembilan director, BH Apr 2026). Offences under the Act can be compounded under the Cooperatives (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2010 (s93). I could not reach or verify the s58 text, the 30-day pre-AGM submission rule, the 30 June AGM date or the penalty amounts: the Act PDF and GP26 PDF did not render (503), and Malaymail returned 403.
result.market: About 16,000 registered koperasi, per the claim; the Nov 2019 figure was about 14,000, of which about 4,200 were dormant. The Dec 2024 Bernama/The Sun report gives 7,779 koperasi failing to keep accounts and 2,304 unaudited. Negeri Sembilan alone has 768 registered koperasi, 340 of them inactive (Apr 2026). I did not re-confirm the claim's 9,800 active / 16,009 registered from an SKM statistic.
result.reason: The duty is real. SKM guideline GP26 (Sept 2024) requires each koperasi to have an SKM-approved auditor audit its accounts every year under s61 of Act 502. Dormant koperasi that skip audits and AGMs for more than 3 years risk cancellation (SKM N9, Apr 2026). I could not read the s58 text, the submission deadline or the penalty amounts. Pain is wide: 7,779 koperasi do not keep accounts and 2,304 are unaudited. But others already cover part of the job. MOCCIS SPBK is web accounting built to SKM reporting rules, and p-SKM is a free Excel tool. ANGKASA's recovery division prepares accounts, and SKM grants RM3,000 to RM3,500. The audit itself needs a human approved auditor. Dormant koperasi have no income, so few will pay. I can't confirm that nothing does the core job.

result.competitor: No named Malaysian software advertising Poisons Book, Prescription Book or reg 26A attendance compliance was found in English or Malay searches. Generic pharmacy POS systems exist (Faris Software, cited in a UTHM paper; legacy GS Vision Pharmacy Manager), but whether they print the statutory forms was not checked. MOH systems (PhIS, MyUBAT) are for public facilities, not private community pharmacies. Absence is not proven: these are search gaps.
result.duty: Poisons Regulations 1952 reg 26, replaced by P.U.(A) 155/2025: retail Poisons Book (Form B), Prescription Book (Form C) and wholesale book (Form A). New reg 26A requires the licensed pharmacist to keep a record of each registered pharmacist's engagement/employment and daily attendance (under Act s16(4A)). Records are kept for every sale, so the duty is daily. Not verified: commencement date, Form D/E naming, 5-year retention, penalty amount. The parliamentary PDF was binary and could not be read. The 2022 Act amendment raised penalties (up to RM50,000 / 5 years per DKSH). A UKM thesis abstract says the 2022 amendment allowed fully digital pharmacy records, but I did not open the thesis (503).
result.market: About 5,271 community pharmacies as of 4 June 2022, per pharmarise.com.my (unverified and internally inconsistent; it also cites 3,835). The MOH FAQ points to a state-by-state statistics table that I did not open. The MOH my.pharma licence list (2025) was not opened.
result.reason: The duty is real. Peraturan-Peraturan Racun (Pindaan) 2025, P.U.(A) 155/2025 (ST.164/2025), replaces reg 26: Poisons Book on Form B, Prescription Book on Form C, wholesale book on Form A. It adds reg 26A, a record of each registered pharmacist's engagement and daily attendance. I could not confirm the commencement date, the Form D/E labels, the 5-year retention, the RM5,000 penalty or e-register acceptance, because the PDF would not parse. I found no Malaysian product advertising poison-book compliance. That is weak evidence, since local pharmacy POS systems (e.g. Faris, GS Vision) were not checked. Market is about 3,800-5,300 community pharmacies (unverified 2022 figure). Record-keeping is the most common inspection failure. But POS bundling is a likely risk and willingness to pay is modest, so the score stays at 4.

result.competitor: Local DNFBP-specific products exist, which contradicts the claim's "no local DNFBP-specific product found". (1) HaloCheck.xyz (Verity Intelligence, Malaysia) does BNM AML/CFT CDD and e-KYC. Since 2022 it has served 30+ reporting institutions running over 70,000 checks a month (vendor figures). It has an MOU with the Malaysian Institute of Estate Agents (MIEA) that lets member agents run e-KYC on landlords, tenants, sellers and buyers. Named users include Zerin Properties (an estate agency) and Mahzan Sulaiman (a chartered accountant and chartered secretary firm). (2) Legal Compliance Tech (Kuala Lumpur, founded 2023) is listed in Stanford CodeX TechIndex as covering CDD/KYC, sanctions screening, risk classification, record keeping and regulatory reporting for Malaysian law firms. (3) Global tools such as LSEG Risk Intelligence also target DNFBPs. SSM and MACS run AML/CFT compliance training for company secretaries. I did not confirm whether any product generates the annual DCR or a full STR log, so a gap may remain there, but it is a feature gap rather than a market with no product.
result.duty: Real and in force. Under AMLA 2001 (First Schedule) and BNM's AML/CFT/TFS policy document for DNFBPs and NBFIs (Sector 5), registered estate agents, lawyers and company secretaries carrying out gazetted activities are reporting institutions. Since 30 Dec 2021 this also applies at firm level. Their duties are: CDD on every party to a transaction (for estate agents, under the policy document's REA section); TFS and sanctions screening; STR filing; record keeping; a s.19 compliance programme; and an annual Data and Compliance Report to BNM. BNM Newsletter 01/2026 (27 Mar 2026), as cited by MAICSA, confirms that the AMLA amending Act came into force on 1 Mar 2026. The same newsletter reports Directive Orders issued to estate agents, lawyers, company secretaries and DPMS, and warns of monetary penalties. I did not open the amending Act's text, so the claimed new personal-liability sections (s.83A-83E) are unverified.
result.market: Utusan (Oct 2024) quotes the LPPEH registrar: 3,121 registered estate agents (REA) and 74,545 negotiators (REN). These are individual registrations, not firms, so the number of REA firms is probably in the low thousands. I found no 2025 firm count. I did not find counts for company secretary firms or law firms in this session. For context only, this is roughly 20k+ lawyers and thousands of SSM-licensed secretaries, not verified here.
result.reason: The duty is real and enforcement is tightening: BNM issued Directive Orders in 2026 and the AMLA amendment took effect on 1 Mar 2026. The core job, CDD/e-KYC plus screening and records for estate agents, company secretaries and law firms, is already served by local products. HaloCheck has an MIEA MOU channel and named estate-agency and company-secretary clients. Legal Compliance Tech targets Malaysian law firms. Global screening vendors complete the field. A newcomer would be competing on features, for example DCR preparation, an STR log and a risk-assessment template, in a fragmented market of small firms with low willingness to pay. Distribution through MIEA is already taken. A narrow DCR/compliance-programme add-on might work, but the candidate as stated is not a gap.

Duty is real: Akta 308 requires JKM registration; unregistered operation is liable to RM10,000 and/or 2 years; inspections are reported at least twice a year; a registration plaque is mandatory. No state tool or product was found that does the specific compliance-pack job (approvals checklist, caregiver KAP/ANAK tracking, inspection records). The market is small: about 3,266 compliant taska (year unconfirmed), 409 in Johor, and roughly 500 to 1,000 unregistered. Operators are scattered and fee-sensitive. Generic taska apps (illumine, which is Malaysia-focused, and Classadia) cover fees and parent communication and possibly some compliance reporting, so the niche is thin. Registration is a one-off or infrequent task and a 2012 reply said certificates run 5 years. I did not confirm the March 2026 ANAK change or any pending Act 308 amendment. Weak recurring pain and a small market.

result.reason: The duty is real. P.U.(A) 99/2024 (OSH Plant Requiring Certificate of Fitness Regulations 2024) puts lift duties on the owner or JMB. The owner must appoint a DOSH-registered competent firm. The certificate of fitness is valid 15 months (The Star, Sept 2026; DOSH DG quoted in Sinar Harian). Frequency is low (15 months). No lift count was found; the market is probably thousands of JMB/MC bodies, with weak willingness to pay.

Not confirmed or refuted. The sector is real: the Malaysia-China protocol was signed Nov 2025 (about RM1.5bn a year), and 16,731 swiftlet houses were registered by 2021. The DVS state system MyWalet (blockchain registration and traceability, used nationwide since early 2022) probably covers registration and traceability, which is much of the core job. I found no commercial swiftlet compliance software, only a UNIMAS student prototype and generic farm tools. I could not find the farm-level record-keeping duties, the penalties, or the 2026 GACC status. The buyers are fragmented, and the free state tool plus the lack of a clear recurring filing weaken the case. A niche add-on (record keeping, audit prep) is possible but unproven.

Duty is real. Act 304 (AELB) and the Basic Safety Radiation Protection Regulations 2010 require licensed medical and dental X-ray premises to have a qualified RPO(M), use AELB-approved personnel dosimetry (TLD/OSL), and hold a facility licence. MOH's Medical Radiation Surveillance Division licenses health facilities, and an MOH circular dated 20 Aug 2025 made RPO training mandatory. I found no Malaysian software for clinic licence, dosimetry or RPO record tracking. Weak points: I could not confirm the renewal cycle, penalties or number of premises. The duty is narrow and sits with MOH and dosimetry providers (Nuclear Agency, Sinaran Utama, Alypz), and it has low frequency and little pain. Score 3.

EUDR is EU law, not Malaysian. Small Malaysian collectors and dealers have no direct legal duty. The duty falls on EU operators, who pass data requirements down by contract. EU dates are now 30 Dec 2026 for large operators and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small enterprises, so they are not the "Dec 2027" the claim cites. Palm is covered by state systems, and mandatory MSPO certification for FFB dealers started 1 Jul 2025. Rubber has the government system MSNR Trace. I found no cocoa-specific source. Buyers are fragmented smallholders with low willingness to pay. Vendors such as TraceX already sell collector and smallholder onboarding. Not a recurring statutory workflow, and I could not size the market.

Duty is real: Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 require KKM-recognised food handler training (SLPM) and typhoid vaccination (reported 3-yearly); owners are compounded (49 compounds for premises employing handlers without typhoid records; Ramadan 2024 notices). Enforcement is heavy (910 of 63,784 inspected premises closed; ~94k handlers inspected, 84.7% vaccinated). No Malaysian tracking product found in Malay or English searches, only generic HACCP apps (GoCanvas, Alcomo). Weak points: owners are thin-margin, staff churn is high, a spreadsheet or WhatsApp does the job, and the MVP is easy to copy. Registered-premise count was not found. FoSIM scope unchecked. Typhoid frequency comes from secondary sources. Score 4.
